newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-BOWE TO JOIN U.S. MARINES.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BOWE TO JOIN U.S. MARINES.

text.p: Former heavyweight boxing champion Riddick Bowe has found a surefire way to get into better shape.
The 29-year-old Bowe announced on Thursday that he will join the United States Marine Corps Reserves and will report to Parris Island, South Carolina, on February 10 for an eight-week boot camp.
Bowe said his stint in the reserves will not end his boxing career.
The three-year commitment includes bootcamp as well as one weekend a month with a reserve unit. Bowe said he plans to return to the ring after boot camp and will fight again at the end of the year.
Bowe, who has appeared less-than-fit for several bouts and often allows his weight to balloon between fights, said being a U.S. Marine has been a lifelong dream.
"This is something I have wanted to do all my life," Bowe said. "Now, I am looking forward to becoming a Marine with the same determination and commitment that made me champion."
Bowe completed enlistment processing this week at the Baltimore Military Entrance Processing Station.

"During the enlistment process Riddick Bowe was screened and found to be mentally, morally and physically qualified for enlistment," said Captain David Steele of Marine Corps Recruiting Command in Washington, D.C.
Bowe (40-1-1) last fought December 14, when he was awarded his second successive disqualification win over Andrew Golota. Golota was disqualified on both occasions for low blows.
Bowe defeated Evander Holyfield in November, 1992 to capture the undisputed world heavyweight title. He lost his titles back to Holyfield a year later.
